newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B share index falls at noon on Lujiazui.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B share index falls at noon on Lujiazui.

text.p: Shanghai B share index was weaker at midday on Friday on heavy selling of real estate developer Lujiazui and trading was dominated by local investors, with foreigners absent due to Christmas, traders said.
The index lost 0.891 points or 1.33 percent to 65.86 points, on volume of 9.5 million shares worth $4.7 million. Of 42 B shares, 40 traded, with 20 down, 12 up and eight flat.

Brokers said local investors sold Lujiazui after the value of its existing shares had been diluted by a three-for-10 rights issue. A total of 60 million additional Lujiazui B shares from the rights issue were listed on Thursday.
They said that heavy profit-taking of market barometer Lujiauzi pushed the index down, with falls of A shares also causing liquidation selling.
Lujiazui traded the most, ending the morning down $0.034 or 2.55 percent to $1.298, on volume of 1.4 million shares.
"Lujiauzi had a big impact on market sentiment, with most domestic investors making their decision to buy or sell based on its performance," one broker said.
"The movement of A shares should have little impact on B shares in the afternoon and drastic falls of B shares are unlikely," a second broker said.
"The index will find strong support around 63 points, with market fundamentals improving and share prices comparatively cheap," he added.
Hotel group New Asia was the biggest loser because of its comparatively high price, falling $0.038 or 8.11 percent to $0.430, on volume of 153,000 shares, brokers said.
Shanghai A shares fell on profit-taking and liquidation selling after rebounds in the past couple of days, with sentiment still unstable, brokers said.

The A index lost 20.525 points or 2.13 percent to 942.353 points, on volume of 250.2 million shares worth 2.0 billion yuan. The SSE 30 blue-chip index dropped 43.990 points or 1.79 percent to 2417.011 points.
Fujian Yaohua was the biggest loser on institutional selling, falling 0.60 yuan or 7.05 percent to 7.90 yuan, on volume of 4.1 million shares.
